passage: Tuesday. At the family dinner in Bhopal, Uncle asked, "Mahima, twenty-five now, when do we eat your wedding sweets?" Mahima put down her fork. "Not yet, Uncle. I'm building my architecture practice." His eyebrows rose; she went red and changed the subject. Friday. Her cousin Asif rang. "Mama is telling everyone you're too fussy." Mahima breathed out. "I'm not fussy. I'm busy, and I'm happy. If that changes, you'll hear it from me first." The next Sunday, when Uncle started again, Mahima smiled. "I know you care. My answer is the same: not yet. Come and see my first site instead." Uncle blinked, then laughed. "Fine. But I'm bringing sweets to the site."

qa.q: On which day did Asif ring Mahima?
What was Mahima feeling at the first dinner, and how did it show?
qa.a: She was embarrassed and flustered. She put down her fork, went red and changed the subject.

qa.q: What changed between Tuesday and the following Sunday in how Mahima answered?
qa.a: On Tuesday she went red and changed the subject. By Sunday she smiled, kindly said "not yet" again and invited Uncle to see her first site.

qa.q: How does Uncle seem to take Mahima's steady answer on Sunday?
qa.a: He blinks, then laughs and agrees, promising sweets at the site, so he seems to accept it and feel included. 🙂

grounding: A young adult who wants to build a career faces questions about marriage and, over several days, holds a clear, steady boundary.

passage: You ask why I never felt sorry for being single at twenty-five, Nilesh? Sit, I will tell you. I am Kavitha, and back then I was a young nurse in Mysuru, just through a hard year when I lost my mother. Every relative asked, "What age now? When will we hear the shehnai?" My father called me to the verandah and said the proposals were piling up. I was trembling, but I said, "Appa, I need two years, for work and for myself. I will tell you when I am ready, and I will tell you if I never am." He was silent a long time. Then he said, "Then I will tell them you have work to do." My aunt clicked her tongue for months. I did not mind. I chose my time, and it was mine.

qa.q: Where was young Kavitha working as a nurse?
qa.a: Kavitha was working as a young nurse in Mysuru.

qa.q: How did young Kavitha feel as she spoke to Appa on the verandah?
qa.a: Kavitha was trembling and nervous, yet steady about what was wanted: two years for Kavitha's own work and needs.

qa.q: What choice did young Kavitha make on the verandah that shaped what followed?
qa.a: Kavitha told Appa calmly that two years were needed and that Kavitha would say when ready, instead of just agreeing or arguing.

qa.q: How did Kavitha's father seem to feel about the request?
qa.a: After a long silence he agreed and offered to tell the relatives that Kavitha had work to do, which suggests he was thoughtful and willing to support the choice.

grounding: A young adult chooses to wait to marry, states the boundary clearly to family, and shows that the delay was a choice.
